review_reference: UNSIGNED DRAFT: awaits the owner's signature of 0168 and 0169 and of runtime-grants.sql at the sha256s in files. Numbers provisional (closed up at integration in release order). Release order (Rahman, #258 7175579690, accepted in 7177085826): 0154, APPT-1, BILL-1, then ED-1, one department per release, so ED-1 ships after APPT-1 and BILL-1, on a staging that holds them. ED-1 Emergency department board and triage (Release D, the department sprint the owner approved on 25 November 2026), built at the recommended option of each open question, not yet answered by the owner: Q-ED-1 A (an ED patient is a row of the live waiting list plus an ED record), Q-ED-2 A (0169: the front desk arrives and sees the board without the complaint, nurses also triage, clinicians and doctors also record the disposition), Q-ED-3 A (an emergency search's patient may be put on the board while the member's own break-glass grant for them is active; Rahman's conditions in #337 7175564791: the arrival's audit row names the grant, consentGrantId, now done, and the DPO accepts facility-wide visibility for the stay, still the owner's and the DPO's), Q-ED-4 A (a complaint of 1-120 characters, never shown to the front desk, never in an audit row), Q-ED-5 A (two-step disposition), Q-ED-6 A (admission requests kept on the ED record until wards ship), Q-ED-7 A (no new write basis). The board reuses 0135's live five-level triage scale, which the clinical lead must sign off before real patients use it. ehr-api's ED_BOARD_ENABLED stays off in production until the clinical lead's checklist and the owner's go-live. runtime-grants.sql is Release E's signed file (49b378f5..., signed 25 November 2026 with 0152 and 0153) plus 0168's block, which grants the 11 entry points to hid_ehr_runtime and takes back the schema-wide sequence grants on the history's identity sequence (ehr.ed_attendance_events_sequence_no_seq) from hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; 0169 adds no grant and is unchanged at 9aa42c47... (Rahman: can be signed as it is). Since Rahman's check of db83d733 (#337 7175564791) and the agent review's round 1 (ed-r1), 0168: a cancel closes only the ED record and keeps the waiting-list row open (a row moved from the outpatient waiting list put back as it was; the row the arrival made back to waiting with no level and no assignee), so a check-in that claimed the row after the arrival is not undone; the history's sequence is the owner's alone (post-checked; runtime-grants.sql revokes it); post-checks in 0148's and 0152's form (owners, row-level security enabled and not forced with no policy, the four triggers by tgtype, tgattr, tgqual, tgnargs, tgfoid and tgenabled, the 18 functions' SECURITY DEFINER setting, volatility, body md5 and search_path, EXECUTE, the validated CHECK, and no waiting-list row written, read from the transaction's own row counters instead of two md5 snapshots of every row); a TRUNCATE guard on the history; no 0149 or 0150 marker and no lock on auth.role_permissions; md5 pins of 0135's check-in and 0145's decision on an unknown record; the guard lets through only the close of an inactive patient's board row; the board card's chart_blocked check names the patient on the directive version. The board's marker (hid.ed_board_closing, the waiting-list row's id as text, set transaction-local by the caller right before its UPDATE of ehr.visit_queue and cleared to '' after) is unchanged, and the mirror's body is unchanged at the md5 ADT-1's 0171 pins (6aaaeb33d1318136fb7fba5ad405fc8e). Runbook (Rahman's item 3 and the board-off nit, in 0168's header and both contracts): before rolling ehr-api back past this image, switch ED_BOARD_ENABLED off on it and clear the board's patients through the waiting list; before switching the board off, hand over the decided admit_requested records outside the board. Rahman's final check of this head is pending.
